Subject: SLA template: target uptime and monthly credits

Ben —

Thanks for sending over the draft SLA earlier. Our legal and SRE teams reviewed it and have a few open items before we move to signatures:

- Baseline uptime: the draft lists 99.9% as the standard. For our production traffic we need to understand the path to 99.95% (what additional commitments or pricing tiers would that require?).
- Monthly remedy / credit ladder: we prefer a cap at 25% of the monthly bill and would like clearer language on how credits are calculated (per-incident vs aggregated monthly).
- Maintenance carveouts: need an explicit scheduled maintenance allowance and a notification SLA (72 hours notice preferred).
- Latency SLO for inference endpoints: can you confirm typical p95 numbers and whether a latency breach would trigger credits or only availability breaches?

I attached an annotated copy with inline comments (SkyRun_SLA_annotated.docx).

Can you share a clean redline that reflects your standard baseline and any enterprise upgrades? If we can get a proposal for 99.95% as a paid uplift and the credit cap language tightened, I think legal can move quickly.

Thanks —

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T12:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template: target uptime and monthly credits

Tom —

Appreciate the thorough review and the annotated doc. I've attached our standard SLA proposal (Redwood_SLA_Proposal_v2.pdf) and summarized our positions below so we can align quickly: 

1) Baseline uptime
- Hosted (standard tier): 99.9% monthly uptime.
- Enterprise uplift: 99.95% available as an add-on (requires a committed monthly spend and dedicated routing pool). I can share a pricing delta after I confirm your target commit.

2) Remedy / credit ladder (monthly aggregated)
- < 99.9%: credit = 10% of that month’s service invoice
- < 99.5%: credit = 25% of that month’s service invoice
- Credit cap: our standard cap is 100% of monthly bill for exceptional months.
- That said, we are open to contractually capping at 25% for enterprise deals; this is a commercial exception and will need approval (see below).

3) Maintenance carveouts and notifications
- Scheduled maintenance not to exceed 8 hours/month by default; we provide a minimum of 72 hours notice for planned work that could affect availability. Emergency maintenance is logged and communicated within 2 business hours.

4) Latency SLOs
- Latency is measured separately; p95 for our hosted LLM endpoints for typical text-gen workloads is ~200–350ms depending on model & sequence length.
- We do not currently tie latency breaches directly to monetary credits in the base template; we can include a latency credit for specific critical endpoints (requires metrics/export hook and SLA monitoring integration).

Next steps: I can make a redline that (a) keeps our standard 99.9% baseline, (b) adds an enterprise uplift path to 99.95% with pricing to follow, and (c) offers a one-time commercial exception to cap monthly credits at 25% (subject to approval). Would you like me to proceed with that redline?

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Proposal_v2.pdf (pdf)

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear summary. We discussed your positions internally and can do the following: 

- Agree to the standard 99.9% baseline for the hosted tier.
- We're interested in the 99.95% uplift as a paid option; please send the pricing delta and any routing/reservation constraints.
- For credits, we can accept Redwood's standard ladder BUT we need the contractual credit cap to be 25% of monthly spend (SkyRun cannot accept a potential 100% credit in a single month). This is non-negotiable for our finance controls.
- Maintenance carveout: we can accept 8 hours/month scheduled maintenance and 72h notice. Emergency patching is understood.
- Latency: we want p95 <= 250ms for our inference /predict endpoint in steady state. Action items for Redwood: please produce a redline that (1) includes a 25% hard cap on monthly credits, (2) offers a priced uplift to 99.95% (commit threshold if any), and (3) provisions an SLI export for p95 monitoring for the /predict endpoint. If we can see that language and the pricing in a redline, we'll route to legal for sign-off.

Appreciate the collaboration —
Tom
